entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request: seen from the front the curl came toward the viewer, so the hands hardly seemed to rise. Source-bound draft from a 3D model turned 50 degrees: standing tall with a dumbbell hanging at each side, palms facing each other; both forearms curl straight up to shoulder height while the upper arms hang still, and lower more slowly to long arms. Each dumbbell stays square to its forearm, as a hammer is held. Dumbbell Bicep Curl is drawn from these frames and turns with it.
entries.summary: Standing with the palms facing each other, curl both dumbbells to shoulder height with the upper arms still, then lower more slowly than you lifted to long arms.

frames.caption: Hold the dumbbells at the sides with the palms facing each other and keep that neutral grip for the whole rep.
Curl to shoulder height with quiet upper arms.
Keep the thumbs up through the rep.
Lower slower than you lifted, back to the natural long-arm position.
Hold the elbows quietly beside the ribs.

entries.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
entries.summary: Standing with the palms facing forward, curl both dumbbells to shoulder height with the upper arms still, squeeze as the wrists turn a little further, then lower slowly to straight arms.
entries.instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length, elbows close to the body and palms facing forward. Keeping the upper arms still, curl the dumbbells up to shoulder height. Squeeze, then lower slowly until the arms are straight.
entries.cues: Elbows stay beside the ribs. Upper arms stay still. Lower slowly.
entries.coachingIntent: Curl two dumbbells with the palms facing forward.
entries.reason: Derived from the Hammer Curl pose table (derivesFrom 62): a palms-forward grip changes how the dumbbells are held, not the motion. Redrawn with its base on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, from a 3D model turned 50 degrees, so the dumbbells lie across the body and tilt at the top, little finger toward the same-side ear. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.

captionOverrides.p1: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length, elbows close to the body and palms facing forward.
captionOverrides.p2: Keeping the upper arms still, curl the dumbbells up to shoulder height.
captionOverrides.p4: Lower slowly until the arms are straight.
captionOverrides.p5: Elbows stay beside the ribs. Upper arms stay still.

Start closing the elbows; the upper arms stay pinned beside the ribs.
The bar comes up in front of the thighs, elbows still behind it.
Curl to shoulder height with the upper arms quiet.
Hold the top, elbows behind the bar and in front of the ribs.
Fight the bar down slower than it went up.
Back to the long-arm rest position, ready for the next rep.

entries.summary: Standing with the palms facing in, curl one dumbbell to shoulder height with the upper arm still, lower it slowly until the arm is straight, then curl the other side.

Lower slowly before the other arm starts.

Pause. Upper arm stays close to the body.
Lower along the same path.

entries.summary: Standing tall with a barbell against the thighs in a shoulder-width underhand grip, drag the bar straight up the torso while letting the elbows travel back behind the ribs, then lower along the same contact path.

Keep the bar touching the torso and let the elbows drift back.
Lower along the same contact path.
Keep the bar touching the torso and lower along the same line.

Pause with the palms facing down and the upper arms still.
Lower slowly until the arms are straight.
Palms face down throughout and upper arms stay still.

entries.name: Zottman Curl

entries.summary: Standing with dumbbells at the sides and upper arms quiet beside the ribs, curl up with the palms turning up, rotate to palms-down at the top with the elbows closed, lower slowly through the overhand grip, and turn back to neutral at the bottom.

frames.caption: Stand with dumbbells at the sides and keep the upper arms quiet beside the ribs.
Curl with the palms turning up while keeping the upper arms quiet beside the ribs.
At the top, rotate to palms-down while the elbows stay closed.
Lower slowly through the overhand grip.
Turn back to neutral only at the bottom.
